subject: Connectivity strategy for EdgeWorks private deployment (VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <msingh@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Connectivity options for EdgeWorks private deployment

Maya — thanks again for the time earlier. To kick off the design review, I wanted to capture the three primary connectivity patterns we'll evaluate for your private deployment: VPC peering (direct CIDR routing), AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints / endpoint services), and site-to-site (S2S) VPN (IPsec).

Can you confirm the following items so we can map trade-offs concretely?
- Expected daily request volume and steady-state qps (tokens/sec is OK)
- Latency SLOs for inference (p50/p95 targets)
- Whether control-plane traffic (model updates, metrics) needs the same path as data-plane requests
- Any strict egress IP requirements (static NAT IPs) or IP whitelisting needs
- Compliance constraints (SOC2/HIPAA) that would affect allowed topologies

Quick notes on what we'll evaluate:
- Throughput and latency: peering often gives lowest latency but requires non-overlapping CIDRs and cross-account routing controls; PrivateLink minimizes internet exposure but can add per-ENI overhead; S2S VPN is easiest for customers with legacy firewalls but may add jitter and NAT complexity.

I've attached our current network diagram and a blank inventory worksheet to capture your subnets and egress appliances. If you can fill the inventory and share, we'll produce a short options matrix and cost delta estimate.

Proposed next step: 30-min technical sync Wednesday to walk the inventory and confirm a PoC plan (10k request run). Are you available 8/5 10:00am ET?

Thanks,
Diego
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference

Diego — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers:
- Volume: baseline ~350 qps, expected peak bursts up to ~1.6k qps during batch windows.
- Latency target: p50 < 20ms, p95 < 60ms if possible.
- Control plane: model uploads and metrics should be on a separate management channel if possible; we'd like data-plane (inference requests) isolated from internet paths.
- Egress IPs: we have an existing NAT fleet and require a stable outbound IP range for upstream partner whitelists (we can provide them).
- Compliance: HIPAA + SOC2 in-scope; prefer minimal internet exposure and auditable flows.

Preliminary preference: PrivateLink looks attractive because it keeps traffic off the public internet. Concern is cross-account routing constraints and potential rate limits on ENIs if we host many endpoints per AZ. We're open to peering for control-plane if that reduces complexity for updates.

I'll populate the inventory (edgeworks_inventory.xlsx) and send it back by EOD. Wednesday 8/5 10:00am ET works for us.

Maya — great, thanks for the fast turnaround and the inventory sheet. Attaching an initial cost/latency sketch (connectivity-costs.csv) and a short options matrix I started.

High-level synthesis (based on the inventory):
- PrivateLink (primary): Meets the "no public internet" requirement and aligns with HIPAA/SOC2 goals. Pros: minimal network exposure, simpler firewall rules on your side (allow endpoint ENIs). Cons: ENI limits by AZ may require throughput planning; small per-GB charges and per-ENI management.
- VPC Peering (control-plane only): Good for administrative/control traffic (model pushes, metrics). Pros: low latency, no NAT required; Cons: requires non-overlapping CIDRs and careful cross-account IAM routing policies.
- S2S VPN (fallback/burst): Useful if you cannot provision PrivateLink in all AZs or need a quick temporary tunnel. Pros: fast to set up; Cons: variable latency and jitter, NAT/eIP complexity, less auditable than PrivateLink.

Recommendation (draft):
1) Primary data-plane: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints per ingest region) to ensure traffic never traverses the public internet.
2) Control-plane: VPC peering between Redwood control VPC and EdgeWorks management VPC for model artifact sync and metrics.
3) S2S VPN: Maintain as a warm standby for DR and burst overflow.

Open items we need from EdgeWorks before finalizing the design:
- Confirm AZ coverage requirements (do you require multi-AZ inference endpoints?)
- Confirm the exact egress IP CIDR for any upstream whitelists
- Any GovCloud or region constraints (you said US-only but confirm)

I'll capture the above in the PoC plan and share a one-page SOW for procurement.

Diego
attachments: connectivity-costs.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <msingh@edgeworks.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T14:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Connectivity options for EdgeWorks private deployment

Diego / Team / Maya — tagging security items we need to lock down if we go the PrivateLink + peering hybrid: 
- Auditability: PrivateLink flows are not visible in the same VPC FlowLogs as peering — plan for flow export on the endpoint ENIs and centralized log aggregation (we'll propose a CloudWatch/Athena pattern).
- KMS & key management: If EdgeWorks will encrypt at rest with their own KMS, we need cross-account key grants for model artifacts (control-plane peering path).
- Egress & NAT: PrivateLink keeps inbound traffic private, but any outbound calls from hosts (callbacks, telemetry) will still need NAT; make sure those IPs are included in your whitelist.
- Endpoint scaling: Request a throughput plan for PrivateLink ENIs per AZ; if you expect sustained 1.6k qps with 1KB payloads, we should model ENI counts and CPU offload.
- STIG/HIPAA notes: Ensure we capture retention periods for logs and access review cadence in the SOW.

I'll attach our security checklist (security-checklist.pdf). For PoC, recommend we run initial tests in a single AZ with PrivateLink to validate latency and ENI behavior, then expand to multi-AZ only if throughput/availability require it.

KM
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
attachments: security-checklist.pdf

Maya — thanks for the inventory and the sync earlier. Pulling the thread together into an operational recommendation and next actions: 

Recommendation (final draft):
- Primary: PrivateLink-based ingress for inference traffic. Rationale: best fit for HIPAA/SOC2 requirement to avoid the public internet and provides strong access controls per endpoint.
- Control-plane: VPC peering for model artifact sync and metrics (low-volume, low-latency). Peering keeps artifact transfer fast and avoids per-GB endpoint fees.
- DR/Burst: Maintain an S2S VPN as a warmed tunnel for overflow and as an interim path during cutover.

Operational notes:
1) PoC: 1-AZ PrivateLink ingest with 100k request run during a weekday peak window. Measure p50/p95 and ENI saturation. (Redwood owns load generator; EdgeWorks will provide subnets and NAT config.)
2) Security: Redwood will provide the endpoint ENI ARNs and CloudTrail events for review. Kim to coordinate KMS cross-account grants.
3) Procurement: attached is a SOW stub for your procurement and legal to review (redwood_sow_stub.docx). We can template in SLAs and retention terms.

Next steps / dates:
- EdgeWorks to provide final egress IP list and completed inventory by 08/07 EOD.
- Redwood to deliver PoC plan + SOW by 08/08 COB.
- Schedule PoC kickoff: target week of 08/16.

If this looks good, Maya, please confirm and we'll open the HubSpot deal stage to "PoC" and loop in procurement.

Thanks — talk soon.
Ben Carter
